Subject: Request: Order form redline + SOW gap analysis

Hi Markus,

Thanks for the demo last week — our engineering and procurement teams are aligned on moving forward but we've run into a couple of gaps between the order form you sent and our implementation expectations. I've attached the order form and SOW with inline comments (two PDFs).

Top-line asks:
- Can you provide a consolidated change order rather than requiring an MSA amendment? Our procurement prefers smaller, order-level adjustments where possible.
- We need clarity on implementation fees (one-time vs. included) and acceptance criteria for the integration milestone.
- Are there rollback/termination mechanics tied to the data retention exhibit? We need a clear runbook.

Can you do a short gap analysis and propose language we can route back to our legal team? We are hoping to close this by the end of next week.

Attachments: acme_marked_orderform_v1.pdf (annotated), acme_marked_sow_v1.pdf (annotated)

Best,

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>

Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Request: Order form redline + SOW gap analysis

Jamie — thanks for the annotated docs and the clear asks. I'm looping in Laura (legal) and Karthik (sales ops) to help us move quickly. Initial read shows three things we should address in a single change order (not an MSA amendment):

1) Implementation fees: several line items in the SOW look like one-time professional services. We'll break them out as a discrete "Implementation Fee" line on the change order and clarify whether they are refundable on failed acceptance.

2) Acceptance criteria: we'll propose a short, measurable acceptance checklist for the integration milestone (API availability, sample traffic test, runbook handoff).

3) Data retention and rollback: we'll add explicit rollback windows and a limited-scope runbook reference in Exhibit C so there's no ambiguity.

I'll do a gap analysis and attach a short notes doc for your team to review. If this approach looks good to you, we'll prepare a tracked-change change order and run it through DocuSign.

Attachment: mk_gap_notes.docx (internal notes — will send a clean copy for review)

Next step: Jamie, can you confirm if Acme's legal prefers change orders to reference the MSA by exhibit ID (our preference) or by full clause excerpt? That will determine how we format the document.

Thanks — Mark
Markus Klein
Head of Sales — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: markus.klein@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, connor.obrien@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-14T08:49:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: Order form redline + SOW gap analysis

Markus / team — I reviewed Jamie's annotated docs and Markus's notes. High-level legal suggestions (I drafted tracked text in the attached file):

- Change order vs. MSA amendment: I agree a change order is cleaner here. We'll reference the MSA (MSA §1.2 and Exhibit C) and include a one-paragraph affirmation that all unchanged MSA terms remain effective. That avoids broad amendment language.

- Implementation fee language: propose a non-refundable "Onboarding Fee" unless acceptance fails due to Redwood's material breach; in that case, fee pro rata refundable.

- Acceptance criteria: include a 5-day acceptance window after a joint test. If acceptance criteria are not met, Customer may request remediation; if remediation fails after two attempts, termination rights for the affected SKU only.

- Data retention/rollback: add a 30-day rollback hold for customer data and a short cross-reference to our standard Data Handling Addendum (Exhibit D).

I've attached redwood_redlines_acme_v2.docx with language suggestions. Connor — can you confirm any operational constraints around a 5-day acceptance window and the proposed remediation attempts? Karthik — once Ops confirms, I'll prepare a change order draft for Jamie's team.

Attachment: redwood_redlines_acme_v2.docx
